g31p.comment: It mostly restates the press release with little named attribution, and its what-changed section misrepresents actuals as prior guidance.

errors: "Summer of Extras" is listed as a new mention, but Adam Rymer cited Summer of Extras on the Q1 call.
"Manager coverage across 14 peak day parts and turnover" is listed as dropped, but Boatwright discussed GM and crew turnover and manager deployment in this call's prepared remarks.
fable.comment: It is the most complete and insightful, with sharp guidance deltas such as the Q2 guide against actual results, HEAP timing and Singapore, plus fair Q&A reads, but it runs long with multi-clause bullets.

errors: "HEAP" is listed as a new mention, but the high-efficiency equipment package was discussed at length on the Q1 call.
"Hourly turnover" is listed as dropped, but Boatwright said crew turnover has returned to historical norms on this call.
sonnet.comment: Concise, well attributed, and strong on the Q1 comparison and evasions, with minor what-changed slips.

errors: "HEAP restaurants producing two to four extra entrees in Max 15" is wrong; both Boatwright and Rymer said two to three entrees, and two to four hours refers to labor efficiency.
In the Brian Vaccaro exchange, "HEAP restaurants do two to four extra entrees in Max 15" repeats the same error; Rymer said "two or three entrees."
Danilo Gargiulo's answer is read as "answered directly", but Boatwright said "I have nothing to report today" on remodel returns, and the unanswered list is empty.
"Tatted Like a Chipotle Bag" is listed as a new mention, but the Q1 call already referenced the tattoo BOGO.
g35fl.comment: It misstates the HEAP throughput figure and leaves the FY comp raise from flat out of what-changed; the guidance list is bloated, attribution is generic and the unanswered list is empty.

errors: "Leadership hires" is listed as dropped, but Boatwright discussed the new Chief Digital Officer Arlie Sisson and Chief Brand Officer Fernando Machado at length on this call.
haiku.comment: Accurate, with useful prior-quarter context in the metrics, but guidance and what-changed are padded with non-changes and the note runs long.

errors: "HEAP" is listed as a new mention, but the equipment package was discussed on the Q1 call.
"Hourly turnover and staffing" is listed as dropped, but this call cited crew turnover returning to norms and consistently high staffing levels.
It ties digital growth to "the protein trend", but in that answer Boatwright referred only to "an emerging trend" without naming protein.
opus.comment: Tight, well attributed and investor-focused, with solid risks and evasions, but its what-changed section has small slips.

errors: Tami Zakaria Q&A attributes the excavator answer to Chris Seibert; Brent Norwood gave the excavator update.
Kristen Owen Q&A attributes the Q4 margin bridge (no refunds, seasonal R&D and SA&G) to Chris Seibert; Brent Norwood said it.
Chad Dillard Q&A attributes the 30%-35% rental figure to Chris Seibert; Brent Norwood said it.
'Dealer inventories for model-year 2023 and 2024 high horsepower tractors declined nearly 40%' – Deanna Kovar was describing late-model used inventory, not specifically dealer inventory.
g36f.comment: Figures are clean and the guidance changes are well tabulated, but several Q&A answers are misattributed to Seibert, and it omits the industry outlook revisions and most of the deflected questions.

errors: Chad Dillard Q&A places the 30%-35% rental and dealer fleet expansion points under Chris Seibert's answer; Brent Norwood said them.
fable.comment: The most complete and accurate note, covering industry guide changes, net tariff math and a well-grounded tone shift, but it runs well over the length target with repetition across sections.

errors: Tone shift says Q3 'cited completed EOP data'; Deanna Kovar said the sprayer and planter programs are still open.
Tami Zakaria Q&A places the excavator answer under Chris Seibert; Brent Norwood gave it.
Chad Dillard Q&A places the 30%-35% rental figure under Chris Seibert; Brent Norwood said it.
opus.comment: Strong, compact note with a full guidance-change table and fair deflection list, marred by minor attribution slips and a mischaracterization of the EOPs as complete.

errors: Tone shift says Seibert repeatedly said it is 'too early to tell on 2027 mix, Europe and pricing'; he did not say that about pricing, only about mix, Europe and Brazil.
sonnet.comment: Accurate, with well-separated Q&A attributions and fair reads, but the what-changed section omits the Europe, construction and C&F price revisions, and some quote choices ('Things can turn quickly.') are low signal.

errors: What changed: 'PPA net sales guidance revised from trending toward bottom end of prior range' – the prior guide was down 5%-10%.
What changed: 'PPA operating margin guidance revised from narrowed range to 11% to 12%' – the prior range was 11%-13%.
Dropped topics lists 'IEEPA tariffs', but IEPA refunds ($110M in Q3, $382M YTD) were discussed on this call.
Risk 'European market and dairy segment mixed conditions' – dairy and livestock were described as stable and favorable.
'Early order programs for U.S. planters and sprayers' – the programs are North American; Kovar said U.S. was trending better than Canada.
Jamie Cook Q&A read 'answered directly', but no 2027 pricing figure was given.
g35fl.comment: Omits the 14.4% margin, gives no attribution in most sections, garbles the guidance comparisons, contains a typo, and lists only one deflected question.

errors: Calls the European policy the 'EU capital budget policy change'; the question referred to the CAP budget policy.
haiku.comment: Solid figures and guidance moves with mostly correct Q&A attribution, but it uses 'Management narrowed or raised' and odd '(not stated)' filler in the metrics.

errors: Risk 'Fourth-quarter margin contraction in Production & Precision Ag and Construction & Forestry driven by seasonally high R&D and SA&G' – Brent Norwood named PPA and Small Ag & Turf.
'dealer fleet expansions representing 30% to 35% of earthmoving transactions' – Norwood said 30%-35% of all earthmoving transactions start as a rental, not dealer fleet expansion.
Angel Castillo Q&A read 'answered directly' – no margin direction was given and the $2-3B lifecycle figure was not addressed.
FTC answer 'rather than altering lifecycle business dynamics' – Norwood said the agreement will help support long-term lifecycle aspirations.
Tone shift 'subdued, multi-year recovery in 2027' – 'multi-year' was not stated on the call.
g38f.comment: Broad coverage, but it relies on 'Management reaffirmed', misstates the Q4 margin segments and the rental figure, and has an overgenerous Q&A read.

errors: Andersen exchange attribution is garbled: "Salmaan Allibhai, Chief Analytics and Technology Officer, Chief Underwriting Officer; Chief Analytics and Technology Officer". Allibhai's only title is Chief Analytics and Technology Officer.
Guidance says Petrucelli "expects a slight uptick in reinsurance commissions". He said "You could see a slight uptick", which is a possibility, not an expectation.

Dropped topics lists "Expense advantage vs growth trade-off in prepared remarks". In Q1 this came up in Mark Hughes's Q&A question, not in prepared remarks, and Q2 prepared remarks still cite the low-cost advantage.
haiku.comment: Solid and well-sourced, with good prior-quarter comparisons and a sharp 'crisis is over' tone note, but it omits the -5.9% pricing index, uses 'Management said' and has a garbled title.

errors: Key takeaway attributes to Salmaan Allibhai the view that AI efficiency gains could offset higher reinsurance ceding commissions. Bryan Petrucelli, CFO, said this.
In the Singzon Q&A, the reinsurance and commission answer is attributed to Allibhai. Petrucelli answered that part.
In the Andersen Q&A, the casualty loss trend and social inflation answer is attributed to Stuart Winston. Salmaan Allibhai gave it.
"The combined ratio was 75.5% for the quarter, compared to favorable prior year loss reserve development of 4.5 points". The 4.5 points was a component of the combined ratio, not a comparison.
Cohen's trough question is read as "answered directly". Winston said there is "no telling where it's going to go in 2027."
g35fl.comment: Multiple misattributions, empty guidance and unanswered sections, and no mention of the buyback expansion make this the weakest note.

errors: "net investment income grew 19.9% quarter-over-quarter". Petrucelli said "in the second quarter over last year", which is year over year.

Getsov Q&A says Kehoe "noted Kinsale will accept lost volume if pricing or terms cross profitability limits". Kehoe said nothing like this in that answer; similar language came from Winston's prepared remarks.
Andersen Q&A attributes the mid-single-digit casualty loss trend to Stuart Winston. Salmaan Allibhai said it.
Singzon Q&A puts the expense-ratio baseline and commission comments under Allibhai's name. Bryan Petrucelli said them.
Hughes Q&A attributes the point that small account property is more stable to Kehoe. Stuart Winston said it.
Cohen Q&A says "selective non-admitted opportunities remain elsewhere". Winston said some business flows to the admitted market but not pervasively.
Guidance says Kehoe "maintained" the 20% ROE target, while its own what-changed section says the target "shifted" from low 20s.
g36f.comment: Numbers are mostly right, but the Q&A is riddled with misattributions and invented content, every answer is read as direct, and no deflections are listed.

errors: Cohen Q&A says Kinsale is "finding pockets of opportunity to grow in general casualty type business". Winston said "We're starting to see some more competition around general casualty type business" and mentioned pockets of opportunity separately.
g31p.comment: Accurate on headline numbers with a reasonable dodged list, but guidance and what-changed are thin (dropping 'Vanguard VYM' is trivial) and most takeaways and risks lack named attribution.

errors: Hughes Q&A says Kehoe "confirmed repurchases will remain the primary capital allocation outlet using the full $337 million authorization". Kehoe never said the full authorization would be used.
Guidance says Allibhai "expects casualty loss cost trends to remain in the mid-single digits". He described the current trend ("probably mid-single digits") and made no forward expectation.
Hughes Q&A is read as "answered directly". Kehoe said he had no insight into when property equilibrium would come.
g38f.comment: Covers the main numbers but misses the pricing index, leans on 'management' attribution, calls every answer direct with an empty unanswered list, and includes some invented specifics.

errors: Risk bullet says "Accident year loss ratio could drift up over time with mix shift from property to casualty, per Kehoe". Salmaan Allibhai said it could drift up.
Hughes Q&A, headed under Kehoe, includes "the loss ratio could drift up over time but losses remain below expectations" without naming Allibhai, who said it.
fable.comment: The most comprehensive note, with excellent what-changed detail (index switch, reinsurance renewal, ROE wording), but it runs long and misattributes the loss-ratio drift comment to Kehoe.

opus.comment: Accurate, well-attributed and insightful, with fair reads, a correct dodged list and a sharp tone shift; it is somewhat long, and it ties the overall -5.9% index loosely to commercial property and derives $87M where Kehoe said about $80M.

errors: Hughes Q&A says "Kehoe said ... Inland Marine is seeing more competition". Stuart Winston said this; Kehoe only interjected "Inland Marine."
sonnet.comment: Tight and well-structured, with six good Q&A exchanges, fair deflection calls and useful what-changed items; one minor misattribution.
